steps.title: Show the current time on the home page as an ISO 8601 string
steps.intent: On the home page, determine the current time and render it as a human-readable ISO 8601 date-time string in the operator's local timezone, current as of the moment it is shown.
steps.acceptance: The home page renders a non-empty ISO 8601 date-time string in the operator's local timezone whose value matches the operator's browser current time within 3 seconds; it is never empty, never a UNIX epoch or other non-ISO format, and never in the future or more than 3 seconds stale at the moment observed.
steps.stand_in: ISO 8601 local-time representation with UTC offset at second precision, e.g. "2026-08-23T16:50:09+01:00" (no milliseconds); local timezone resolved from the browser per runbooks/domain-expert/common.md ("Timestamps display in the operator's local timezone") and issue #40. Pending q-iso-format and q-refresh.

verification_targets.check: The rendered time string is non-empty.
The rendered string parses as a valid ISO 8601 date-time and is not a UNIX epoch integer or other non-ISO format.
The parsed rendered time equals the operator's browser current time within a 3-second tolerance and is not in the future.

boundary_cases.description: If the time source yields no value, the view must not render an empty string; it refuses with a setup hint instead.
If the displayed value would be more than 3 seconds behind actual wall-clock at the moment observed, it is refreshed/re-rendered rather than shown stale (behavior depends on q-refresh).
If the system/browser clock is unavailable or returns an invalid or future value, the view refuses with a hint rather than showing an invalid value or UNIX epoch.
At the day boundary the ISO date portion rolls over correctly (23:59:59 advances to the next day 00:00:00) in the local timezone.
